When each state burned in 2025, and where this week sits

Weekly crop-fire detections, 15 Sep – 14 Dec 2025 (grey line). The orange dot is this week's 2026 count. Each panel has its own scale, because the point here is timing.

Surplus against burning

Each dot is a state: surplus residue (Mt a year) against crop-fire detections in Oct–Nov 2025. The shaded corner (orange dots) has at least 10 Mt of surplus and 1,500 fires: collection pays off most there.

Fires: NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m, type 0, nominal/high confidence. Wheat-season (Apr–May) burning is in each state's profile.

First-generation ethanol · feedstock and food

Blending rose fast, capacity rose faster, and grain filled the gap

The ESY 2026-27 tender asks for about 1,100 crore litres, bars cane juice and B-heavy molasses, and cuts the maize price. These charts show where that leaves feedstock, food and capacity.

Where the handover lists put each plant

Handover lists (2020–23): sugar-mill distilleries, SAMARTH co-firing plants and pellet vendors, SATAT CBG, 2G ethanol. DFPD approvals are not drawn (one point per state).

Audit by source list

A shared point is a coordinate reused by plants with different names, usually a town or district centre. A mismatch is a point that falls in another district or state than the one listed.

Flagged plants: the point falls in another district or state
About the data

Open data, open code

Three notebooks rebuild this page from public sources: 01_data_hub_state_index_atlas, 02_satellite_residue_pilot and 03_build_webapp, in the india-bioenergy-observatory repository. The programme's tasks, challenges and research agenda are in the separate report.
